No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Minimum Pension: PenCom to Expand Beneficiary List Beyond 173,209 by Bukola Aro-Lambo 10 seconds ago in Business Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The number of Nigerian retirees eligible for the N52,500 Minimum Pension Guarantee is expected to rise beyond the initial 173,209 beneficiaries as more contributors with inadequate retirement benefits leave active service, with the National Pension Commission (PENCOM) projecting an automatic review of eligible pensioners.
Head of the Corporate Communications Department at PENCOM, Ibrahim Buwai told LEADERSHIP that the initial beneficiaries include retirees who contributed for at least 240 months, equivalent to 20 years, but receive pensions of about N20,000 because they retired early when salaries were significantly lower.
The 173,209 pensioners benefiting from the newly introduced Minimum Pension Guarantee (MPG) are now being paid N52,000 monthly pensions. The beneficiaries comprise 34 per cent retirees from the federal government, 12 per cent from state governments and 54 per cent from the private sector.
According to Buwai, the number of beneficiaries are expected to rise as more people whose pension fall around N20,000 retire. It is expected that the addition to the beneficiaries list would be automatic with their retirement.
Section 84(1) of the Pension Reform Act provides for the Minimum Pension Guarantee, stating that all Retirement Savings Account holders who have contributed to a licensed Pension Fund Administrator for a number of years to be specified by the Commission shall be entitled to a guaranteed minimum pension as may be specified from time to time by the Commission.
The provision leaves the determination of the qualifying contribution period to PENCOM.
The Director-General of the National Pension Commission (PENCOM), Omolola Oloworaran, while unveiling the programme for the distribution of funds under the initiative at the launch of the Presidential Pension Security Initiative in Abuja, said the Federal Government had set aside about N400 billion as Pension Protection Fund to finance the guarantee, describing the intervention as a landmark measure to protect retirees whose monthly pension payments fall below the approved threshold.
“The figure was not plucked from the air; it has been validated by an actuary, and it is subject to review. And it is funded,” Oloworaran said.
The PENCOM boss, however, explained that state governments must contribute to the N400 billion Pension Protection Fund before their retirees can benefit from the guarantee. She said the requirement was designed to ensure the sustainability of the scheme.
Meanwhile, Executive Director of the Centre for Pension Rights Advocacy, Mr Takor Ivor, commenting, said the Minimum Pension Guarantee should not be restricted to the 173,209 retirees identified by PENCOM.
According to him, the guarantee should cover every retiree whose monthly pension is below N52,500.
Ivor said the intervention was a welcome development, particularly given the hardship faced by pensioners who currently receive as little as N20,000 monthly.
